articleTitle: Frequency Domain Signal-to-Noise Ratio Pre-Processing for Fault Classification in Planetary Gear Systems Using Audio Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Rotating machines commonly used in industries, such as planetary gears transmission systems, emit acoustic signals that contain significant information relating to the equipment's condition. Thus, the acquisition, processing and analysis of these signals are interesting procedures to enable the machine's working state monitoring. Given this scenario, we propose a technique for fault classification of planetary gear systems, based on a Frequency Domain Signal-to-Noise Ratio (FDSNR) pre-processing algorithm, applied over the audio signals emitted from the gear system. The processing procedure feeds Supervised Machine Learning models such as Artificial Neural Networks and XGBoost. For our practical experiment, a planetary gear system was built in the laboratory, using a set of 3D-printed plastic gears and physical components and structures used for fixation and assembling purposes. By printing some anomalous gears, we could make replacements to alternate ordinary gears with anomalous ones, providing three different conditions for the apparatus: one normal configuration, and two anomalous conditions induced by a mass imbalance caused by the defective gears. Our final approach used: a microphone and an audio interface for acoustic capturing and audio recording; acoustic processing techniques that extract the key features from the audio files; and machine learning models that use these features to perform fault classification. The final experiment using the approach achieved a peak accuracy of 98% with an XGBoost model.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Radiometric Localization Techniques Based on the Intensity of the Received Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the efficacy of radiometric localization techniques for partial discharges sources, utilizing received signal strength. Tests in experimental setups with dimensions ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\times 4\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> with two different sources to emulate the phenomena were employed: a controlled source and an oil cell. In addition, the envelope detection was evaluated for this purpose. The techniques based on amplitude made the detection and localization of PD sources more practical and feasible. The location errors are around 0.25 m indicates that these techniques are promising and could help to reduce the costs associated with partial discharges monitoring processes.

articleTitle: Assessment of an Instrumentation System for Radiometric Monitoring of High-Voltage Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper provides an evaluation of an instrumentation system designed for the detection, classification, and localization of partial discharge sources. It discusses improvements made to the previous system, which faced limitations in resolution for detecting signals. The study describes comprehensive tests performed to characterize the system components and preliminary tests for specific applications, including testing multiple systems for partial discharge localization and detection of signals from different pieces of equipment.

articleTitle: Effect of Ground Clearance Reduction in Chip Antenna for IoT Micro-PCBs
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In order to find solutions for miniaturizing printed circuit board (PCB) area in products for the Internet of Things, a comparative study between different ground clearance sizes in a same chip antenna is presented. Two micro-PCBs intended for a Bluetooth Low Energy system-in-package have been designed, using the same commercially available microcontroller, transceiver, and chip antenna. On one board, the clearance area around the antenna followed the manufacturer's recommendations and, on the other, a non-copper area was left only immediately below the antenna. A development board has also been designed to compose a complete system. Measurements of received signal strength indicator, latency, and throughput have been taken in a controlled environment and in the field to evaluate the quality of the communication in both cases. Radiation patterns of both PCBs have also been plotted. The micro-PCB without ground clearance shows a surface saving of 12.23% and a suitable enough performance for short-range communications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Quadcopter Body Frame Vibration During Hovering Flight with Variable Rotor Speeds
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Quadcopters and other propeller-driven vehicles and machinery experience periodic vibrations that can impact their performance and longevity. However effective implementation of vibration reduction techniques requires accurate identification and characterization of these vibrations. This paper presents an analysis of the measured vibration of a quadcopter in hovering flight under varying propeller speeds and fit of parts. To collect data, four accelerometers were placed on the drone's arm, with an additional accelerometer positioned inside the center of the frame. Sampling was conducted at a frequency of 1 kHz using a myRio-1900. The collected data from four flights was subsequently analyzed using time-domain graphs and spectrograms from the Gabor transform. Results indicated a prominent presence of blade pass frequency and its harmonics, alongside asynchronous vibrations observed during flights with loosely fitted components.

articleTitle: Artificial Inteligence Based IoT Systems and Data Processing for Monitoring Flow in a Water Supply Network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The technological development of water distribution systems is essential to improve the population's living conditions, as well as improving management within companies in the sanitation sector. In this context, seeking efficient ways of monitoring and forecasting demand constitute promising alternatives to detect hydroenergy losses and reduce system operating costs. In this work, a methodology based on Typicality and Eccentricity Data Analytics and artificial neural networks is proposed for use in an experimental monitoring node, to estimate, indirectly, the water flow in a laboratory water distribution system. As a result, proposed system was able to forecast future flows with MAPE under 5% and MSE under 0.0003.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of LoRaWAN Network in Landfill
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)

authors.preferredName: João Paulo Silvino Belo da Silva

abstract: LoRaWAN is a network protocol characterized by low latency, long-range wireless transmission reaching distances of tens of kilometers, and low power consumption of end devices (nodes). These properties favor the application of this technology in various fields related to the Internet of Things, such as environmental monitoring. This article presents methodological strategies for implementing and analyzing a wireless sensor network based on LoRaWAN technology in a landfill to promote future monitoring of system variables. Therefore, a radio station consisting of a LoRaWAN gateway was installed. Physical variables that could influence the proper functioning of the network were considered, such as physical location and specification of the LoRaWAN gateway antenna, obstacles between devices and data transmission parameters. Finally, the analysis of the network performance in the landfill indicated that the most significant issue pertains to the shaded areas resulting from the irregular terrain.

articleTitle: A Filtering Perspective to SAPF Control for Current Harmonic Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Shunt active power filters (SAPF) are a tool for suppressing the harmonic content present in the electrical grid, caused by nonlinear loads. An important part of this system is the SAPF control, where the filter is controlled in order to supply the harmonic currents required by the loads. In this paper, we show that this control system, usually performed by pre-estabilished controllers tuned in the relevant frequencies, works as a measurement of the harmonic content in the electric power system (EPS) by means of band-pass filtering, in order to reinject it in the right amount. This new perspective indicates that the choice of quality factor of the band-pass filter may impact the result of the harmonic compensation in several ways, and can thus be used as a parameter for control design, as shown by simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of a 1.85-4.3 GHz LC-VCO in 65 nm CMOS Technology for L-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an LC-VCO with complementary cross-coupled structure-based core topology for wide tuning range frequency generation (from 1.85 GHz to 4.3 GHz) for application in a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL)-based frequency synthesizer with extended frequency coverage. From layout level simulation by applying a 65 nm CMOS technology, the results indicate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PN}{@}1\mathrm{M}=-104.4\ \text{dBc}/\text{Hz}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\text{out}}=4.0\ \text{GHz}$</tex> and tuning range = 79.7%.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Signal Conditioning Circuit Based on Envelope Detection for the Detection of Partial Discharges in UHF
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The radiometric acquisition of partial discharges in the UHF spectrum requires acquisition equipment with high sampling rates and bandwidths, which makes detection more expensive. The use of signal conditioning circuits to reduce the acquisition hardware requirements is a practice with the potential to decrease the price of monitoring the quality of electrical insulation by partial discharges. However, the signal conditioning circuit electronic components should be characterized for the efficient phenomenon detection, since the strengths and weaknesses of the each one of these components can be detected, improved, and even combined to obtain a more effective monitoring system. In this way, the characterization of a partial discharge detection system, that uses a signal conditioning circuit based on envelope detection, is performed in this work to verify the operability of the selected electronic components for this purpose. The partial discharge detection is performed by a Circular Printed Monopole Antenna (PMA) and the signal conditioning circuit is composed by filter, low noise amplifier (LNA) and a Schottky diode-based envelope detector. The transmission coefficient of filter was measured, the figures of merit of LNA like transmission coefficient, noise figure and 1dB compression point were measured. Furthermore the envelope detection was verified with the frequency spectrum of conditioning signals. The proposed circuit was able to trace the envelope of partial discharge pulses and reduce their acquisition rate by 87 times.

articleTitle: Manufacture of Planar Interdigitated Capacitive Sensor and RVE Model Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Capacitive sensors hold significant promise for biosensors in both gaseous and liquid environments, enabling the detection and monitoring of biochemical compounds through variations in sensor capacitance. This paper aims to manufacture a capacitive sensor and validate its Representative Volume Element (RVE) computational model, aiming to optimize the sensor in future work. The sensor was manufactured using Computerized Numerical Control (CNC) laser, employing a planar geometry with a 15-finger interdigitated capacitor and FR4 dielectric. The sensor capacitance value was measured in different mediums (air, water, ethanol, and various water-ethanol solutions) using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). The RVE model was adapted and simulated using Comsol Multiphysics software, validating its behavior and ability to accurately represent the sensor with an error margin below 10%. This study demonstrates the feasibility of using the RVE model to optimize capacitive sensors and highlights the importance of simulation software and techniques such as Finite Element Method (FEM) in biosensor development.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Thermoelectric Waste Heat Recovery in a Commercial Vehicle: Real Case Versus Simulation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Energy harvesting is the process of converting available environmental energy into electrical energy. In our daily lives, many things — such as vehicles and industrial machines and pieces of equipment — do not utilize all their input energy for doing work, releasing the remaining energy to the environment as heat, for example. As an example, Heavy-Duty Vehicles (HDVs) are used globally to transport loads and a significant amount of thermal energy from HDV's internal combustion engine is lost as heat through their exhaust system. A way to capture this heat is using a semiconductor Thermoelectric Generator (TEG) that converts directly heat into electrical energy. Some studies have experimentally analyzed the large-scale use of TEGs on HDV's exhaust system to harvest energy considering a combination of TEGs connections. As it is possible to explore different TEG connection combinations, but it is very expensive to evaluate all different combinations, this paper proposes a way to simulate different combinations of TEGs based on a proposed SPICE-based TEG model. The obtained result shows that using the proposed simulation approach, it is possible to evaluate a specific combination before testing it in practice.

articleTitle: Constant Temperature Difference Thermoresistive Radiometer with Enhanced Thermal Link
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The paper discusses and analyzes an improved structure radiometer that operates with a thermoresistive sensor. The proposal aims to enhance the heat exchange pathway between the thermistor and its surrounding medium. SPICE simulations were conducted to assess the impact of this modification, with a focus on response time and sensitivity. The proposed modification reached an improved response time and sensitivity. Moreover, temperature control based on a feedback linearization technique was deployed to reduce energy consumption, improving the radiometer's energy performance.

articleTitle: Development of an Open-Closed Eye Detector of Alternative Communication for Users with Severe Disabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Efforts to enhance autonomy for people with disabilities have become a focal point of medical and academic research. Alternative communication methods aim to improve independence and quality of life for individuals with severe disabilities. However, many existing approaches are costly or complex, limiting access for many patients. In this paper, we developed an open-closed eye detection system using the ESP32-CAM microcontroller, which is affordable, independent, and computer-cost-effective. Our hypothesis suggests that by analyzing a grayscale image, we can determine if an eye is open or closed just using an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 120$</tex> vector dimension, rather than processing all 19200 image pixels. Our results achieved a 100% success rate for the experimental group, validating our proposed approach and hypothesis.

articleTitle: Microcontrolled System to Map and Monitor Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in Pasture Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The vast territorial extension of Brazil is also a positive factor, but there is room for improvement through technological implementations. This work proposes monitoring the vegetation index (NDVI) by mapping the state of the pasture during the cattle's stay in the field. Measurements obtained with a commercial Greenseeker device are compared and integrated with values extracted from satellite images from the Satveg tool, which has a periodicity of 16 days and a resolution of 250 meters. A function is created to predict the NDVI in the total area based on points collected locally and from the satellite, using the KNN and Kriging algorithms for data fusion and interpolation. The article foresees contributions to the efficiency of agricultural production, allowing correct livestock management based on NDVI mapping. Additionally, results from previous simulations of analog circuits are presented for developing the NDVI measuring instrument. Future work aims to use the embedded system to automatically collect NDVI data and generate the Map presented here.

articleTitle: Cloud Battery Management System Development
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Batteries are vital in many modern applications, from portable electronic devices to electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Its correct operation is essential to guarantee safety, optimized performance, energy efficiency, and reduced costs over time. To this end, the BMS (Battery Management System) plays a fundamental role as it performs cell monitoring, state estimation, load balancing, thermal control, and charge and discharge control activities. However, these devices' low processing and data storage capacity are significant limitations. To solve this problem, a new hardware and software approach has been developed and used in management systems, such as the cloud BMS. In this new architecture, processing power and data storage capacity availability grows exponentially. This work presents the development of a hardware and software solution for a cloud BMS, based on the ESP32 IoT module. A board was built for this, and a software system using the AWS IoT platform was implemented. After discharging a 48 V battery bank, the voltage, current, and temperature parameter monitoring functionality was verified.

articleTitle: Integrated LDO Regulator for Wireless Energy Harvesting in Internet of Things Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work focuses on the development of a Low-Dropout Voltage Regulator (LDO) powered by radio frequency at 2.45 GHz, with an 1.8 V output, designed using 130 nanometer CMOS technology, targeted for low-power applications such as Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The aim was to create an efficient circuit adaptable to the growing needs of IoT systems, where energy efficiency is crucial. Minimum sensitivityof −8 dBm was achieved, indicating the circuit's ability to handle low power levels of radio frequency efficiently. This work aims to contribute to the development of efficient and sustainable energy solutions capable of supporting RF-powered IoT devices, expanding the possibilities of application.

articleTitle: Concrete Crack Detection Using Embedded Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this work, we present an embedded AI model for real-time concrete crack detection, considering the trade-offs between model complexity and accuracy. For this purpose, we implemented Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 CPU and we analyzed inferencing time, peak RAM usage, flash usage, and metrics such as precision, accuracy, recall, and F1 score. The research provides a quantitative comparison between MobileNet versions 1 and 2, and two CNN models with different numbers of layers, aiming to create an efficient and accurate solution for crack detection on surfaces of concrete structural members used in civil infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Stimulation and Measurement System for the Characterization of Graphene FET Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents the description of a system developed to automate the procedures for stimulation, measurement and electrical characterization of a Graphene Field-effect (GFET) biosensor which was developed aiming the diagnosis of viral infections in the point of care. The paper describes the structure of the biosensor, how its electrical characterization can be used to identify a virus and presents the arrangement built to stimulate and measure its electrical response. Next, we describe the test procedures and the methods to construct the GFET characteristic curves. We explain how the presence of virus genetic materials reflect on these curves and present an example of identification of Zika virus. The system allows the extraction of several parameters that can be used to automate the diagnosis, which is part of the investigation in progress.

articleTitle: Integrated Multi-Mode Modem in a 130 nm CMOS Process Using Open Source Design Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The growing expansion of the open source technology in the development of integrated circuits democratizes the access to full silicon design flow. In this context, this article discusses the development of a digital-type integrated circuit using a fully integrated design flow with open-source tools in a 130-nanometer CMOS process. The digital circuit used was a Multi-mode modem based on software defined radio, capable of supporting amplitude (ASK), frequency (FSK), and phase (PSK) modulation and demodulation schemes. Digital design flow concepts and open source EDA tools were used, complemented by functional checks to ensure accurate and efficient performance of the integrated circuit. The GDS layout was generated with the rules that meet the requirements of the manufacturing process, validating the design of the integrated circuit and the performance of the open source process.

articleTitle: New Approach for Airflow Modulation to FOT and Pulmonary Secretion Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Excessive accumulation of mucus occurs due to various situations or pathologies, such as Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, post-COVID-19 sequelae, or general cases of pneumonia, bronchiolitis, and other respiratory problems and different techniques can be used in respiratory physiotherapy. However, problems with generating airflow signals up to 40 Hz, sanitizing difficulty, and low biocompatibility of the used materials, hinder the applicability and validation of new approaches and methodologies. In this paper, we evaluate a new approach to airflow modulation using a system with high biocompatibility, easy production and assembly, and high consistency on the airflow signal frequencies. Airflow signals with different frequencies and pressure levels are considered in the experiments, then, we analyze the energy associated with each frequency component of the generated signals to evaluate the system and its applicability for respiratory physiotherapy.

articleTitle: Centroid-Guided YOLO for Plant Stem Detection in Digital Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This study focuses on the utilization of a YOLO (You Only Look Once)-based object detection approach, along with the development of a customized algorithm, to address the identification and localization of invasive plant stems within agricultural crops. The initial phase involved the creation of a dataset comprising 485 manually annotated images, sourced from three distinct data repositories. Subsequent to this, the YOLO model underwent training to accurately recognize the plants depicted in the images. Following the model training, an algorithm was devised that leverages the centroid of the G vector in the RGB image as the designated point of interest for precise stem localization. The algorithm's effectiveness was assessed utilizing key metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). For images sized at 600×600 pixels, the resulting MAE and RMSE values were calculated at 34.4 pixels and 46.8 pixels respectively. Notably, these outcomes underscored the necessity for refining the detection process, particularly in instances involving plants with delicate branches, where differentiation between the branch and the image back drop proved challenging. In terms of practical application within agrochemical dispersion systems, it was discerned that dispersion takes place across an application area rather than a singular point. By incorporating the proposed algorithm in conjunction with a dispersion cone aperture measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\times 100$</tex> pixels, it was projected that the dispersion system could effectively cover approximately 92.4% of the existing plants. This algorithmic approach exhibits the potential to curtail agrochemical dispersion by a substantial factor of up to 36 times, yielding economic and sustainability advantages through the reduction of waste and environmental contamination.

articleTitle: Developing an Energy Monitoring System for Small and Medium Consumers: A Step-by-Step Guide
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Currently, energy monitoring and management are indispensable for small and medium-sized consumers, and new approaches in hardware and software are being proposed. This article presents a comprehensive step-by-step guide for designing and implementing a custom energy monitoring system. It integrates an energy meter and a Rogowski coil for current measurement with low uncertainty. By exploring the historical importance and technical advancements of these technologies in the context of related works, the article provides a foundation for the results presented. It covers the system architecture, calibration procedures, device specifications, and firmware complexities in the Materials and Methods section, serving as a roadmap for developers of new energy monitoring solutions. The Developed Prototype section examines calibration and uncertainty evaluation, using ISO G.U.M. as a reference, and offers insights on details such as equipment uncertainty, repeatability, and ADC resolution.

articleTitle: EOG Measurement Analysis Under Different Lighting Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Exposure to different wavelengths of light has been demonstrated to have an impact on the body's physiological processes. This work tests such influence in electrooculograms (EOGs). An analysis associated with the recording of the EOG of six healthy volunteers under five different light conditions is presented. Natural light (at midday and in the afternoon), incandescent, fluorescent, and LED artificial light conditions were considered. A commercial bioamplifier and five electrodes were employed to measure the EOG. Participants were exposed to eight minutes of each light condition after eight minutes of darkness. EOG was recorded during the final four minutes of each light period. The experimental results obtained from the examination of the volunteer's EOG in the temporal and frequency domains show significant differences in the considered parameters.

articleTitle: Application of Wiener Filter and Sparsity Theory for Pulse Unfolding from Scintillator Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This study introduces an unfolding algorithm that integrates the Wiener Filter and Sparsity theory to effectively narrow the width of pulses in time, addressing the challenge of pile-up effects in environments with substantial electronic noise. The algorithm is tested with data from cosmic ray setup experiment that is composed by a scintillator and a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM). The algorithm's performance highlights its potential in improving the consistency of peak positioning and pulse resolution, crucial for precise radiation measurement.

articleTitle: Voronoi-Based Approach to Increase Connectivity and Coverage in Randomly Deployed Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Deployment of sensor nodes is a very critical issue in Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) because it can decrease the quality of service (QoS). Sensor nodes can be randomly deployed over large, hazardous, and inaccessible areas, which can generate redundancies through clusters, isolated nodes, and subnets, creating unmonitored holes in the region of interest (RoI). This deployment problem can be minimized with the use of mobile nodes, constituting a hybrid wireless sensor network (HWSN), to search and integrate nodes by expanding the connectivity frontier region in the direction of the biggest holes identified by the Voronoi Diagram in the RoI. This allows expanding coverage with the mobile node and create new connections with isolated nodes and subnets that are in the neighborhood. However, although several Voronoi Diagram-based approaches are found in the literature, they increase coverage without addressing network connectivity, the focus of this work. Thus, in this paper we propose and compare the Voronoi based algorithm (VBA) and the Voronoi Virtual Force Algorithm (VVFA) to expand the connectivity region of the WSN with random deployment. The results show that the Voronoi approach presented a better performance in a convex environment and similar performance in a non-convex environment concerning coverage and connectivity. The Virtual forces approach possibilities of avoiding obstacles but present a local minimum.

articleTitle: PyBlocks: A Modular Open-Source Simulator for Visible Light Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The PyBlocks Simulator is an open-source tool designed for Visible Light Communication (VLC) systems using a block diagram paradigm. It promotes modularity and reusability by representing system components as blocks implemented in Python. PyBlocks can simultaneously simulate multiple domains, making it suitable for complex systems that require analyzing combined effects across electrical and optical layers. This study validates PyBlocks by comparing its simulated results with experimental data from a real VLC system. The open-source nature of PyBlocks fosters collaboration and continuous improvement, providing a valuable resource for researchers and professionals in the field.

articleTitle: Study of the Generation System-Induced Degradation of Airflow Signal for FOT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)

authors.preferredName: Hélio Matheus Mendonça de Santana Moraes Sampaio
José Gilmar Nunes de Carvalho Filho

abstract: In the forced oscillation technique (FOT), a pressure generator typically delivers a sinusoidal airflow to the patient through an oscillator circuit, which modulates the frequency of the voltage supplied to a speaker. When the speaker-generated airflow interacts with the respiratory system, it causes a forced response in pressure and airflow. This forced response is useful in modeling the system's characteristics using a transfer function. However, system components may degrade the produced signal, compromising the transfer function analysis. This paper investigates an FOT system equipped with a speaker and a pneumotachometer to examine interference with the generated airflow signal. This investigation explores how the generated signal behaves under variations in frequency and amplitude. As a metric of signal degradation, we analyzed the percentage of the signal's energy at its natural frequency and the percentage dispersed among its first harmonics.

articleTitle: Optimization of RF Passive Impedance Matching Networks Using a Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison to low-cost passive impedance matching networks, encompassing three different techniques of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> model: lumped, distributed and hybrid. Additionally, three different optimization approaches including simulation are compared within impedance transformation of a practical case study involving a commercial Bluetooth transceiver and an SMD antenna. The performance of each technique and approach is analyzed in terms of the scattering parameters, the bandwidth of the network, PCB footprint and associated costs. The study underscores the crucial role of electromagnetic simulations in the design of matching networks, due to its reliability. It also exhibits the hybrid technique as the most favorable option, both technically and practically. The results and insights derived from this study contribute to the optimization methods of impedance matching techniques tailored for low-cost FR4 substrate applications in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Implementation and Investigation of the Operation of a SAW Sensor in the Feedback Loop of Sinusoidal Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: SAW sensors find widespread use across various measured quantities, especially in biological or chemical applications. Measurements with SAW usually happen through the open-loop approach, which requires a vector network analyzer to measure the phase and magnitude of the output signal. These devices do not allow automation and integration in multi-sensor systems. An alternative approach called closed-loop offers reduced cost and complexity. In this method, only the frequency is to be observed. Closed-loop circuits implement SAW sensors in the feedback loop of sinusoidal oscillators. Doing so is still a challenge due to the lack of reliable oscillator topologies that resist perturbations in the sensor's surface. In this paper, we design a closed-loop SAW measurement circuit that effectively maintains oscillation when the SAW sensor is included in the closed loop. We compare the inclusion of SAW equivalent models in the feedback loop of our oscillator. We discuss their differences to investigate which SAW model that most accurately represents the response of the real sensor. Our results confirm the effectiveness of our oscillator as part of a sensor, shifting > 100 kHz when the SAW device is perturbed with a drop of water.

articleTitle: Optical Properties Modulation of Porous Silicon Microcavities for Biosensor Application
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Optical sensors and biosensors with response in the visible spectrum region are suitable for integration with excitation sources and detection devices, as laser diodes and photodiodes in the visible region are commercial devices that are easy to purchase from any optical device supplier. In this sense, the present work reports the optical modulation response of microcavity devices based on porous silicon technology, aiming to obtain microcavity response in the visible spectrum region for biosensor application. The optical modulation response of microcavities were obtained controlling the different fabrication parameters such as the doping type of silicon substrate, the number of periods of the Bragg mirror of the photonic crystal, the electrochemical solution, the current density of anodization process, and the anodization time. The results obtained in this work showed that the microcavities response from 1080 nm to 612 nm with quality factor higher than 30. These results showed that microcavities fabricated could be applied successfully to biosensor in the visible region with high optical resolution due their high-quality factor value.

articleTitle: LoRa Multi-Packet Protocol for Image Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Several countries have implemented automatic meter readings to bill basic services. It requires smart meters and the deployment of communication networks (wired or wireless). Several companies offering basic services still use analog meters. Regarding smart meter implementation in Peru, we find that only electricity companies are currently in the trial stage. And the most advanced implementation is using Power Line Communication (Wired Network). The water service is in the project stage and the gas service does not present information. We propose a module that takes a picture of the meter's counter, packages the data, and sends it over a LoRa Network to a Gateway. We implement a LoRa multi-packet protocol prototype for image transmission. The Multi-Packet protocol assigns bytes from the LoRa sub-packet to be the header of the packet, this header gives information to improve efficiency. Sending packets in batches improves energy consumption and time transmission because the sender does not have to wait for an ACK response. This work is the first step in a surveillance system, and gives information about image transmission using LoRa.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulation, SDR Implementation and Commercial Device on LoRa Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The LoRa protocol stands out for its applicability in remote sensing and the IoT. However, this protocol is proprietary and implemented directly on chips developed by its owner, which can hinder performance analysis. In this scenario, the use of Software Defined Radios (SDR) becomes apparent. Therefore, this study verifies the robustness of the LoRa protocol in a Gaussian noise environment using an implementation of the protocol in SDR previously developed for GNU Radio. To achieve this, this paper provides an extensive comparison of simulated, SDR-based, and commercial devices to perform a robustness evaluation. The results confirm the effectiveness of LoRa modulation in negative signal-to-noise ratios and the compatibility of the SDR LoRa implementation with commercial devices, although they reveal discrepancies with the proprietary implementation.

articleTitle: Location Analysis Probing Rockets in Ground with Telemetry Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Rocket launch centers are crucial in technological development across various fields, including meteorology, long-distance real-time communications, geoprocessing, and satellite operations. However, one of the challenges in tracking probing rockets is accurately identifying their position from the moment of launch until the initial seconds, due to ground noise that interferes with traditional radar location systems. In this study is proposed an innovative method to precisely determine the distance between the rocket and the ground telemetry station. We utilize onboard telemetry signals processed by the Acquisition and Processing Data Trajectory (APDtraj) system, developed by Delsis Aerospace for the Launch Center. This system enables the identification of the rocket's position both on the ground and during the early stages of flight, using telemetry data processed by APDtraj. This monitoring equipment alone calculated the distance between the Telemetry Station and the rocket just moments before launch lift-off with an error of only 16.844 meters from the actual position of origin. Based on our studies, we were able to measure the radial distance and location between the rocket and the telemetry station just four seconds after launch, even without reliable radar information, which is often disrupted by ground noise. This technological advancement not only enhances the efficiency of rocket launch operations but also expands overall tracking capabilities.

articleTitle: Compact Airflow Measurement System for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: With the latest COVID-19 pandemic, there has been a notable rise in cases involving patients with respiratory issues. This surge has provoked advancements in pulmonary rehabilitation systems, aimed at preventing the need for intubation. Recent studies also emphasize a growing concern over the probability of future pandemics, primarily targeting the respiratory system. In the current context, while several commercial devices exist, they often lack precise measurements of the volume of air delivered to patients, potentially leading to complications by overlooking crucial aspects of the patient's lung mechanics. Moreover, the high costs associated with these devices further hinder accessibility. Therefore, we propose a validated airflow measurement system to enhance the accuracy of flow measurements provided by such devices. This system is portable, easy to develop, and constructed using accessible components, with most materials feasible for fabrication via 3D printing, machining, and resin molding. Following calibration with an Alharad syringe, the system demonstrated commendable reliability, with over 95% of samples falling within the region of interest. Additionally, the proposed system exhibited remarkable performance, yielding measurement errors of less than 4% for both positive and negative flows.

articleTitle: Development of an Electrical Substitution Pyrheliometer
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The study of solar radiation is of fundamental importance within the context of global climate change and its applications range from understanding the planet's climate to optimizing energy systems. This work describes part of the development of an electrical substitution pyrheliometer to measure solar irradiance using a cavity-type thermal sensor. The pyrheliometer has a total field of view of 5° and can be operated in both atmosphere and vacuum. The blackened Nickel Phosphorus sensor element was fully developed at the institute and has an absorbance greater than 99.9 %. This radiometer will serve as the basis for the development of a pyrheliometer for measuring solar irradiance on board a satellite.

articleTitle: An Open-Source BioMEMS Platform for Generalized Early Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)

authors.preferredName: Thales Vieira e Silva Lobo de Almeida

abstract: Cancer remains one of the most pressing challenges for humanity, with early detection significant for improving survival rates. Open-source initiatives have revolutionized various fields by fostering collaboration, broadening impact, and democratizing access to resources. We propose to expand this ethos to cancer research, introducing a versatile biosensing framework developed using open-source tools only. This biosensor is capable of detecting diverse types of cancer simultaneously, or detecting a single type with enhanced sensitivity. To validate the platform, a proof-of-concept design is presented, and limitations of the current open-source ecosystem are discussed.

articleTitle: A Low-Frequency Sinusoidal Voltage Controlled Oscillator Based on Switched Capacitor Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Low-frequency sinusoidal Voltage Controlled Oscillators (VCO) are used as signal generation modules in instruments for Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS), which has several important applications in contexts such as biomedical and agricultural, for help in the diagnosis of human and plant diseases, respectively. Unfortunately, the design of sinusoidal VCO for low-frequencies has several issues, such as the difficulty of sweep-of-frequency, voltage-to-frequency nonlinearity, harmonic content, and difficulty of integration on a chip. To address this, we propose a low-frequency sinusoidal VCO that uses a square wave VCO to control the frequency of a switched capacitor based oscillator. As proof of concept, a circuit with two commercial Integrated Circuits is implemented in a breadboard and the results are analyzed in terms of Total Harmonic Distortion and input-output relationship for a frequency range from 1 Hz to 12 kHz.

articleTitle: Phase-Controlled Three-Phase Rectifiers Without Grid Synchronization: A New Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Three-phase rectifiers play a vital role in industry, often requiring grid synchronization for proper operation. However, existing synchronization methods typically rely on AC voltage sensors, besides being complex systems. This paper introduces a novel approach to controlling phase-controlled three-phase rectifiers without the need for grid synchronization, and notably, without digital controllers, based only on simple average voltage measurement and a feedback control, thus enabling assembly using only analog hardware. The operational principle is explained, accompanied by a mathematical analysis demonstrating asymptotic stability under specified conditions. Comparative simulations against a conventional synchronization method, the Synchronous Reference Frame Phase-Locked Loop (SRF-PLL), indicate comparable, if not superior performance, with notably improved average settling times. These results suggest that the proposed system could effectively replace SRF-PLL in suitable applications. Nonetheless, further research is warranted to enhance system performance and increase reliability.

articleTitle: Improving Positioning Accuracy for Connected Vehicles: Integration of Low-Cost INS with GNSS
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Nowadays, accurate positioning systems are becoming increasingly indispensable, mainly for applications such as Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAV), Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications, Precision Agriculture (PA), among others. The main technologies used for navigation purposes in those applications are of the Dead-Reckoning (DR)- and Position Fixing (PF)-types. Inertial Navigation Systems (INS) are examples of DR technology that provide solutions at high sampling rates. However, they accumulate errors over extended periods of time. Conversely, the Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) are examples of PF technology, which provide a bounded position solution, with global coverage at a lower sampling rate, but are susceptible to interference and signal losses. One recommended technique to maintain the advantages of both INS and GNSS is sensor fusion, i.e., INS/GNSS integration. This work aims to present practical results obtained with low-cost INS and GNSS receiver integration for CAV applications. The primary contribution is to showcase results of the so-called Loosely Coupled (LC) INS/GNSS integration, which exhibits accuracy improvements (w.r.t. standalone GNSS navigation solution), as validated through dynamic experiments. Tests reveal enhancements of 31.29%, 23.29%, and 21.79% in terms of horizontal, vertical, and total position accuracy, respectively, when compared to standalone GNSS. Moreover, the LC-INS/GNSS strategy can deliver 1.5 meter horizontal and 3.0 meter vertical position solutions at 22,5% and 52,49% of probability, respectively. Standalone GNSS can only deliver 0,42% and 16,32% of probability under the same conditions. These results confirm the relevance of INS and GNSS fusion to achieve CAV application requirements.
